patterns.usage_note: Marks the person or group for whom an evaluation holds, so it is almost always followed by an assessing predicate (大切だ, ありがたい, 難[むずか]しい) rather than by an action the noun performs. Where からすると invites you to reason from that party's position toward a conclusion, にとって simply says who the value judgment is true for. にとっての is the adnominal shape used before a noun (私にとっての宝物); にとりまして is the polite business variant and にとっちゃ the casual one.

examples.ruby: 子[こ]どもにとって、遊[あそ]びは大切[たいせつ]な学[まな]びだ。
examples.english: For a child, play is a vital form of learning.

examples.ruby: 母[はは]にとって、猫[ねこ]は家族[かぞく]の一員[いちいん]です。
examples.english: To my mother, the cat is a member of the family.

examples.ruby: 彼[かれ]にとっての幸[しあわ]せは、静[しず]かに本[ほん]を読[よ]む時間[じかん]だ。
examples.english: For him, happiness is time spent quietly reading.
